newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude steady, looking to test resistance.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude steady, looking to test resistance.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were mostly firmer in early trading on Thursday and traders are looking for a test of resistance above $22.00 later in the session.
At 1115 EDT, crude oil for July delivery was up one cent at $21.87 a barrel.
Products were tracking crude. July unleaded gasoline was up 0.03 cent at 64.90 cents a gallon, while July heating oil was steady at 57.80 cents, up 0.12 cent.
Traders said there was scant fundamental news in Thursday's trade and that most people were concerned with the impact, if any, of another large delivery against the crude contract.

The June crude contract expired Tuesday and NYMEX sources said 2.372 million barrels of foreign crude was delivered against it, of which 2.349 million was foreign, mostly Nigerian Bonny Light. That was near last month's record 2.73 million barrels of foreign.
Apart from delivery, the main focus in crude was on what signs the charts were giving for technical traders.

July crude advanced through the $22 mark at the start of trading Thursday but stalled at $22.08. Traders said the May 19 and May 20 highs of $22.15 had gotten in the way but expected a retest of that point later today.
"The market can't decide what to do with itself now," one broker said. "Everybody's counting the deliveries, trying to figure out who's getting the bonny light."
"I think if the (crude) market doesn't go through last week's high (at $22.43, basis July), then we're going to go lower. It's an interesting situation," he said.
News of another border incursion by Turkish forces into Iraq had supported crude late Wednesday but the impact as the strife there continued was muted by Thursday, traders said.
